intro.title: Next.js App Router Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple multi-page Next.js application using the App Router to understand its core structure. You will learn how to create and navigate between pages using file-based routing, where each folder in the app directory becomes a route. The main technologies involved are Next.js 13+, React, and TypeScript, focusing on the `app` directory, `page.tsx` files, and the `Link` component. By the end, you'll be able to set up a basic Next.js project with multiple pages that users can click through seamlessly.
intro.usecase: The Next.js App Router is the foundation for building modern web applications with organized routing and server-side rendering. You'll use it to create multi-page dashboards like analytics tools or admin panels where each section (users, reports, settings) has its own dedicated route. This pattern appears in e-commerce sites where product listings, shopping carts, and checkout flows are separate pages with optimized loading. As a developer, you'll implement this to structure complex applications with clean navigation, SEO-friendly pages, and efficient data fetching across different views.

objectives: Implement a Next.js application using the App Router structure
Configure dynamic routes with TypeScript type safety
Construct page components with server and client rendering strategies
Initialize and manipulate data fetching within App Router components
Integrate layout components that persist across multiple pages
Apply loading and error states using App Router conventions
Bind navigation between pages using Next.js Link components

steps.title: Import Next.js App Router APIs and React
steps.instruction: Import React and the necessary Next.js App Router APIs including useRouter, Link, and usePathname.
steps.hint: You'll need to import from 'react' and 'next/navigation' for these APIs.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Create the main page component structure
steps.instruction: Create a default exported functional component named HomePage with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return a simple JSX wrapper element (like a div) for now.
steps.hint: Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to export it as the default export and include TypeScript typing for the component.

// Import React and the necessary Next.js App Router APIs here

// Create the HomePage component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A HomePage component is created with TypeScript typing and returns a JSX wrapper element.
successCriteria: The component is named HomePage, has proper TypeScript typing (returns JSX.Element), is exported as default, and returns a JSX wrapper element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named HomePage, has TypeScript typing, is exported as default, and returns a JSX element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a functional component named HomePage with TypeScript typing that returns a JSX wrapper element.

steps.title: Initialize the router hook
steps.instruction: Inside your HomePage component, initialize a router object using the useRouter hook from Next.js.
steps.hint: Call useRouter() and assign the result to a variable named 'router'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: using a hook to get data
const router = useRouter();
steps.expectedOutcome: The router object is initialized and ready to be used for navigation and routing information.
successCriteria: The useRouter hook is called and its result is stored in a variable named 'router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useRouter() and storing the result in a variable named 'router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The router object wasn't properly initialized. Remember to call useRouter() inside your component.

steps.title: Initialize the pathname hook
steps.instruction: Inside the HomePage component, declare a variable named currentPath and assign it the value returned by the usePathname hook.
steps.hint: Call the usePathname hook and store its return value in a variable. This hook doesn't take any parameters.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: using a hook to get current value
const currentUser = useCurrentUser();
steps.expectedOutcome: The currentPath variable will hold the current URL path string, which you can later display in the UI.
successCriteria: The currentPath variable is declared and initialized with the usePathname hook.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling the usePathname hook and storing its return value in a variable named currentPath.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the HomePage component, declare a variable named currentPath and assign it the value from the usePathname hook.

steps.title: Define navigation handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your HomePage component, define a function named handleNavigate that uses router.push() to navigate to '/about' when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls router.push('/about') inside it. Remember to define it within the component body, before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a handleNavigate function that can be called to navigate to the '/about' page programmatically.
successCriteria: A function named handleNavigate is defined inside the HomePage component and it calls router.push('/about').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named handleNavigate and calls router.push('/about').
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleNavigate function is not defined correctly. Check that it's inside the component and uses router.push('/about').

steps.title: Add dynamic route demonstration
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a Link component that navigates to a dynamic route with an ID parameter. Use the route '/users/123' as an example.
steps.hint: Use the Link component you imported earlier. Set the href prop to '/users/123' and add appropriate text content.

<Link href="/products/456">View Product 456</Link>
steps.expectedOutcome: A Link component appears in the UI that demonstrates navigation to a dynamic route with a parameter.
successCriteria: The Link component has href="/users/123" and displays appropriate text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the Link component with href="/users/123" and appropriate text content.
